questions.question: A team is to be selected from 9 girls : A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H and I. C cannot be selected with H. G and F have to be selected together. Only one among D, H and B must be selected. A and D have to be selected together. IF C and G are selected, then what can be the maximum number of members in the team including C and G?
questions.questionHtml: A team is to be selected from 9 girls : A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H and I. C cannot be selected with H. G and F have to be selected together. Only one among D, H and B must be selected. A and D have to be selected together. IF C and G are selected, then what can be the maximum number of members in the team including C and G?
questions.solution:
As per the condition, we have two teams possible.

Team 1: C G F D A E I and Team 2: C G F B E I

Clearly, the maximum number of members in the team including C and G is in 'TEAM I' having '7 members'.

questions.question: Six people P, Q, R, S, T and U are living on a six different floors of the same building. The lowermost floor in the building is numbered 1, the floor above it, number 2 and so on till the topmost floor is numbered 6. R lives on the floor immediately below the floor of P. Q does not live on the topmost floor. T lives on the floor immediately below the floor of S. P does not live on any of the floors below S. Only three people live between the floors of U and T. T and U live on even numbered floors. Who lives on the floor number 4?
questions.questionHtml: Six people P, Q, R, S, T and U are living on a six different floors of the same building. The lowermost floor in the building is numbered 1, the floor above it, number 2 and so on till the topmost floor is numbered 6. R lives on the floor immediately below the floor of P. Q does not live on the topmost floor. T lives on the floor immediately below the floor of S. P does not live on any of the floors below S. Only three people live between the floors of U and T. T and U live on even numbered floors. Who lives on the floor number 4?
questions.solution:
Floor People
6 U
5 P
4 R
3 S
2 T
1 Q

Thus, according to the final arrangement R lives on the floor number 4.

questions.question: Six persons, A, B, C, D, E and F, were born on different dates - 12 th , 14 th , 18 th , 19 th , 4 th and 6 th , of the same month. None of them were born after D and he was born just after E. Only three people were born before A. Only two people were born between C and E. B was not born after C. Who among the following was born on 12 th ?
questions.questionHtml: Six persons, A, B, C, D, E and F, were born on different dates - 12th, 14th, 18th, 19th, 4th and 6th, of the same month. None of them were born after D and he was born just after E. Only three people were born before A. Only two people were born between C and E. B was not born after C. Who among the following was born on 12th?
questions.solution:
The final arrangement is:

4th → B, 6th → C, 12th → F, 14th → A, 18th → E, 19th → D

Hence, F was born on 12th.

questions.question: Directions: In the following question, assuming the given statements to be True, find which of the conclusions among the given conclusions is/are definitely true and then give your answers accordingly. Statement: P ≥ A > I = R; S < A > M. Conclusions: I. M < P II. P > S III. M < R
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: In the following question, assuming the given statements to be True, find which of the conclusions among the given conclusions is/are definitely true and then give your answers accordingly.

Statement:

P ≥ A > I = R; S < A > M.

Conclusions:

I. M < P

II. P > S

III. M < R

options.text: Only I and II are True
options.html: Only I and II are True

options.text: Only II and III are True
options.html: Only II and III are True

questions.solution:
Given: P ≥ A > I = R; S < A > M

On Combining: P ≥ A > I = R; P ≥ A > S; P ≥ A > M

Conclusions

I. M < P → True (as M < A ≤ P).

II. P > S → True (as P ≥ A > S).

III. M < R → False (as P ≥ A > I = R; P ≥ A > M, thus a clear relation between M and R cannot be established)

Hence, only conclusions I and II are true.

questions.question: In this question, a statement is followed by two conclusions, numbered I and II. Find out which conclusion(s) is/are true based on the given statement. Statement: P > R ≥ Q = W ≤ S < E Conclusions: I. Q < E II. R > S
questions.questionHtml:
In this question, a statement is followed by two conclusions, numbered I and II. Find out which conclusion(s) is/are true based on the given statement.

Statement:

P > R ≥ Q = W ≤ S < E

Conclusions:

I. Q < E

II. R > S

options.text: Either conclusion I or conclusion II is true.
options.html: Either conclusion I or conclusion II is true.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II are true.
options.html: Both conclusions I and II are true.

questions.solution:
Given statement: 

P > R ≥ Q = W ≤ S < E

Conclusions:

1) Q < E → True (As, Q = W ≤ S < E gives; → Q < E, So Q < E True)

2) R > S → False (As, R ≥ Q = W ≤ S gives; → There is no clear relation between R and S, So R > S is not True)

Hence, the correct answer is "Only conclusion I is true".

questions.question: Two statements are followed by two conclusions, numbered I and II. Find out which conclusion(s) is (are) true based on the given statements. Statements: P > Q, R ≤ S, Q = S > T Conclusions: I. T < P II. Q ≥ R
questions.questionHtml:
Two statements are followed by two conclusions, numbered I and II. Find out which conclusion(s) is (are) true based on the given statements.

Statements:

P > Q, R ≤ S, Q = S > T

Conclusions:

I. T < P

II. Q ≥ R

options.text: Neither I nor II is true
options.html: Neither I nor II is true

options.text: Both I and II are true
options.html: Both I and II are true

questions.solution:
According to given information:

Given Equation: P > Q, R ≤ S, Q = S > T

P is greater than or equal to Q; R is less than equal to S; Q is equal to S and S is greater than T.

Conclusions:

I. T < P - True (In this conclusion, there are three symbols >, ≥​ and = in between P and T. So, this will be sufficient for this conclusion to be true).

II. Q ≥ R - True (In this conclusion, R ≤ S, Q = S > T given so Q ≥ R. So, this will be sufficient for this conclusion to be true).

Hence, the correct answer is "Both I and II are true ".
